notes: Independently read every eligible production file, including the full Control UI and styles.d.ts declaration, plus package.json and openclaw.plugin.json; expectations were manually authored without Inspector implementation, helpers, output or another fixture.

All 22 files beneath extensions/clawrouter matched the pinned commit byte-for-byte. The partition is 9 production-source files, 2 reviewed metadata files, 6 test-file exclusions and 5 non-source exclusions.

Package metadata declares index.ts and src/control-ui.tsx as shipped entrypoints. The UI type import ../pool.js stays within the plugin root; every other local source import also stays within the root. No additional plugin-owned/shared shipped source boundary was found. Solid dependencies and Node built-ins are outside this SDK audit; installed dependencies were not crawled.

No test-only helper files require an ambiguous exclusion: the six excluded TypeScript files have .test. basenames, import Vitest, and are not imported by production source. The CSS import does not make CSS eligible under the explicit source extension list.

pool-gateway.ts selects registerGatewayMethod through Pick<OpenClawPluginApi, "registerGatewayMethod"> and calls that method. Both type-reference and call apply, so the API member is mixed. The registration callback request/context is a Gateway request, not an OpenClawPluginApi or PluginRuntime handle.

Provider callback contexts, model.api values, the local runtime string in index.ts and the ControlUiHost in control-ui.tsx are not OpenClawPluginApi/PluginRuntime handles. Public control-ui.ts types establish ControlUiHost as a separate browser host contract; its properties are not normalized to api or runtime.

Calls on openAiReplay, anthropicReplay, googleReplay and tool-family objects operate on SDK helper return values. Only the direct imported helper dependencies/calls are recorded; no helper internals or arbitrary returned-member paths are inferred.

Immediately destructured provider-auth-runtime dynamic imports identify resolveApiKeyForProvider without retaining a namespace, so there is no synthetic star export. The readRecord import alias maps to asOptionalRecord.

usage.ts directly references typeof fetchWithSsrFGuard. That SDK export is mixed with import, call and type-reference, while its module remains runtime because every module dependency site is an ordinary value import.

The manifest contracts are top-level providers:clawrouter and contracts.usageProviders:clawrouter. Activation, setup, providerAuthChoices, configSchema, uiCapabilities and controlUi metadata do not add identities under the frozen manifest field whitelist.

No API on/registerHook calls, proven PluginRuntime members, opaque runtime escapes or genuinely unresolved SDK references were found. SDK type dependencies are retained for the source phase; no published-artifact equivalence is claimed.
